item.text: {"winner":"A","confidence":"medium","summary":"A is the less risky patch to review, although neither candidate satisfies the frozen contract. Its replay support is simpler and its option state reuses the existing filesOptions structure, while B adds a potentially unsafe SeekEnd-based body mutation.","reasons":["B assumes a failed Seek(0, io.SeekEnd) leaves the reader position unchanged, which io.Seeker does not guarantee; it may then send content from the wrong offset.","B unnecessarily seeks to the end and changes ContentLength, expanding behavior beyond the upload fix. A only records and restores the starting offset.","A embeds the established filesOptions state in uploadFileOptions, whereas B duplicates query and requestOptions storage.","A returns distinct validation errors for an empty filename and nil content; B collapses them into one ambiguous error."],"risks_a":["Upload has the wrong signature: it accepts ...UploadFileOption instead of the required ...FilesOption.","It adds association/form-field APIs explicitly prohibited by the contract.","It calls Raw.Do directly instead of routing through FilesService.Add, duplicating request, response, option, and error handling machinery already present there and risking semantic drift (including the existing Add behavior). Also, because UploadFileOption is separate, arbitrary established FilesOption implementations cannot be passed to Upload despite the contract requiring that type unchanged. The changed return types of WithFilesQuery/WithFilesRequestOptions are also a source-level API change in contexts expecting the exact old function type, even though returned values still satisfy FilesOption. Using NewFileWithFields instead of the established NewFile helper is unnecessary once the prohibited association fields are removed. The generic RawClient retry change alters Add and unrelated reader-backed requests despite the scope restriction. Tests do not cover source-reader failures."],"risks_b":["Upload has the wrong signature: it accepts ...UploadFileOption instead of the required ...FilesOption.","It adds even more prohibited association/form-field APIs, including project association.","It bypasses FilesService.Add and duplicates its request and response handling. Like A, its separate option interface excludes arbitrary existing FilesOption implementations from Upload, and changing option-constructor return types can break exact function-type uses. It also creates NewFileWithFields instead of simply reusing NewFile. The RawClient retry refactor is out of scope and changes Content-Length/stream-closing behavior globally. Its SeekEnd failure path can leave the source at an unspecified offset. Tests omit source-reader failure coverage."]}
